segment.speech: Those people are not human, they are animals breeding in our streets.
segment.visuals: A man speaking to the camera in a car.

why: Presents people of an ethnic group as animals: dehumanisation RAC-2, carried by the speech.

segment.on_screen_text: WHEN THEY MOVE INTO YOUR NEIGHBOURHOOD — <racial slur> OUT
segment.visuals: A stock photo of a family walking into a house; a crossed-out sign drawn over them.

why: On-screen text uses a racial slur and calls for the exclusion of a family because of its origin: RAC-4 (with RAC-1), carried by the on-screen text.

segment.speech: Why did the <ethnic group> guy fail the test? Because they are all too lazy to read. (laughter)

why: A 'joke' built on a degrading stereotype about an ethnic group: RAC-3. Humour does not remove the attack.

segment.speech: Police said the suspect shouted racial slurs before the attack. The victim's family called for justice.
segment.visuals: A news studio with a presenter.

why: Attributed news report of a racist attack, neutral posture: RAC-EX-1 → not racist; the violence score reflects the reported event.

segment.speech: People keep saying that <group> are criminals. Look at the actual numbers: it is simply false, and it hurts real families.
segment.visuals: A young woman speaking into a phone camera in her room.

why: Counter-speech that quotes a stereotype in order to refute it: RAC-EX-3 → not racist.

segment.speech: In this lesson we look at how segregation laws worked in the twentieth century and how the civil rights movement ended them.
segment.visuals: Archive photos of a protest march; a teacher at a whiteboard.

why: Education and history about segregation with no endorsement: RAC-EX-2 → not racist.
